title: Winter Road
summary: Nine haiku inhabit a dark field that withholds them from a single view. A poem becomes legible through proximity, can be held briefly, then recedes as attention moves elsewhere.
responsibility: a poem can remain hidden until approached
meta_description: Winter Road is a digital haiga space by Mozare in which nine English haiku are found through movement and held only for a time.
hero_lead: Nine English haiku inhabit a dark field. None is presented as the next item in a sequence. The reader searches by moving and finds that another poem can begin to surface elsewhere.

prelude.label: READING CONDITIONS
items: Most of the field remains dark.

views.title: Three views
views.intro: Three images hold distinct reading conditions without reducing the work to a single representative screen.
items: The root phrase appears while the poems remain undisclosed.
A poem becomes legible by degrees before it can be read in full.
One poem remains while another begins to appear elsewhere.

context.title: A haiga space
paragraphs: The nine poems began around two words: winter road. Repeated rewriting moved some words, removed others, and allowed several to return under new grammatical pressure. The result is a family of completed haiku without a single poem serving as the original.
In the browser, the poems coexist without becoming equally available. Darkness gives distance a role, makes discovery local, and lets the field recover after a poem fades.

identity.encounter: Search by proximity; keep by click or tap

motion.provenance: authentic captured states from the released work; assembled without invented interface states
